newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate jumps to 9.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate jumps to 9.8 percent.

text.p: Croatian average money market rate jumped a whole percentage point to 9.8 percent on Monday as demand for kuna funds increased, dealers said.
They said total settlements rose to 78.9 million kuna, of which most were bank loans at rates between 8.0 and 19 percent.
One loan, struck at 25 percent, pushed the average call money rate to 9.7 from 8.3 percent.
Insurers' short-term rates were flat at 7.0 percent.
The weekend overnight trade totalled 66.6 million kuna, mostly thanks to borrowings by banks with shortfalls.
The National Bank of Croatia calculated kuna midrates for Tuesday at 5.4411 to the dollar and 3.5642 to the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
